correctness.rationale: The binary witness has a k-cycle a paired with counter increment 1 and a transposition b with increment 0, with k=alpha+1, h=n+1. The generated permutation projection is S_k. Identity-permutation words a^k and (ab)^(k−1) increment the counter by coprime k and k−1, hence the generated group is S_k×Z/h, INCLUDING k=2, and every B state is reachable/distinguishable. Accepted B words project precisely onto the stabilizer of k. Therefore the quotient final set is all k−1 nonfixed states, and symmetric-group transitivity yields quotient DFA minimality and asc=alpha. All alpha≥m are obtained; the published unary interval 1..mn provides alpha<m; no nonempty K,L can give empty right quotient since permutation transitions are invertible. Independent BFS enumerated the entire action for all 12 (k,h) with 2≤k≤5, 2≤h≤4 and 30 stabilizer/quotient cases. The infinite result follows from the group proof.
risks: The lower range relies on published unary spectrum Corollary 32; this was checked as a real theorem, not inferred from small cases.
No claim of smallest TOTAL-state binary witnesses.

value.rationale: Alphabet-size optimality is a natural sharp refinement of the existing unary-to-nonunary dichotomy. Explicit two-generator group control replaces a previously independent third letter, and the unary interval proves sharpness, so this is structural rather than a renaming of the unrestricted theorem.

final_claim: For all positive input accepting-state complexities m,n, the right quotient of binary permutation languages realizes every positive output accepting-state complexity; if either input complexity is zero only zero is possible, and unary output spectrum is precisely 1..mn.
